name: Flat Zigzag
tagline: Single-level vectorized snake bin-packing: replicate experts globally, then zigzag-assign all replicas directly to all GPUs (no node hierarchy).
pseudocode:
1. Skip the group-to-node hierarchical Stage 1 entirely
2. Greedy replicate experts to total $R$ replicas: at each step, replicate the logical expert with max effective load $w_e/c_e$
3. Compute per-replica tokens $t_p = w_{\ell(p)}/c_{\ell(p)}$
4. Sort all $R$ replicas by descending $t_p$; assign block-by-block
5. Even blocks: pack 0,1,...,G-1; odd blocks reverse to G-1,...,1,0 (zigzag)
6. Inverse-permute back to original replica indices to produce the final phy2log/log2phy/logcnt tensors
diff_from_baseline: Variant introduced for this benchmark: drops the group-to-node decomposition (Stage 1) of EPLB and uses a single global zigzag pass. Faster than hierarchical methods but ignores inter-node topology; tests whether locality-aware packing matters at this scale.

name: Greedy (DeepSeek EPLB)
tagline: Original DeepSeek EPLB with Python for-loop greedy bin-packing: items sorted by weight, each placed in the lightest under-capacity bin.
pseudocode:
1. Stage 1 - groups to nodes: greedy bin-pack groups onto nodes by descending group weight, picking the lightest pack with capacity
2. Stage 2 - replicate experts: greedy add replica to logical expert with max effective load $w_e/c_e$
3. Stage 3 - replicas to GPUs within node: greedy bin-pack replicas onto GPUs by descending tokens-per-replica
4. Each greedy step uses a Python for-loop over batches and items
5. Compose final phy2log via inverse permutations
6. Build log2phy mapping by scattering replica indices
diff_from_baseline: DeepSeek-AI EPLB (2024); DeepSeek-V3 Technical Report (arXiv:2412.19437). The original open-source EPLB implementation - correct hierarchical greedy bin-packing but slow (~540ms on medium configs) due to Python iteration.

name: Zigzag (vectorized hierarchical)
tagline: Hierarchical EPLB with vectorized zigzag/snake bin-packing replacing the inner Python loops; Stage-1 and Stage-3 use PyTorch tensor ops.
pseudocode:
1. Stage 1 - groups to nodes: sort groups by descending weight, then zigzag-assign to nodes (even blocks 0..N-1, odd blocks N-1..0)
2. Permute logical experts so each node gets contiguous group_size experts
3. Stage 2 - replicate experts within each node: greedy LPT (kept as for-loop) until replicas_per_node
4. Stage 3 - replicas to GPUs within node: zigzag bin-pack by descending tokens-per-replica
5. Compose inverse permutations to recover global phy2log
6. Scatter to build log2phy and logcnt
diff_from_baseline: Cheng et al. 2025 (Barbarians at the Gate, Section 5.2). Internal frontier-lab EPLB variant that replaces Stage-1 and Stage-3 greedy for-loops with a vectorized zigzag tensor pattern, ~20ms on medium configs while preserving hierarchical structure.
